question: A does half as much work as B in three-fourth of the time. If together they take 66 days to complete the work, how many days shall B alone take to do it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of efficiencies of A and B = (1/2) ÷ (3/4) = 2 : 3.

Total combined efficiency = 2 + 3 = 5 units/day.

Total work = Combined efficiency × Total days = 5 × 66 = 330 units.

Time taken by B alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of B = 330 ÷ 3 = 110 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 110 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A does half as much work as B in three-fourth of the time.

Together they complete the work in 66 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let B take x days to complete the whole work.

⇒ A completes half the work in (3/4)x days.

⇒ Time taken by A for full work = 2 × (3/4)x = 1.5x days.

⇒ Let Total work = LCM of 1.5x and x = 3x units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 2 + 3 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Time taken together = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ 66 = 3x ÷ 5

⇒ 3x = 66 × 5

⇒ 3x = 330

⇒ x = 110 days.

⇒ B alone takes x = 110 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 110 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency and time are inversely proportional when the total work is constant.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the total amount of work done by each individual. If workers work for the same number of days, their wages are divided exactly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is mathematically identical to Time & Work. The only difference is that an outlet pipe or leakage works with a negative efficiency (it empties the tank), while an inlet pipe works with a positive efficiency.
